response.consequence: Legacy storage drifts out of sync with unified storage on writes, and the dual-write guarantee in mode 3 is lost. Rollback to an earlier mode would then expose stale or missing data.
response.explanation: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection now run the legacy write in a goroutine. Each goroutine derives its context with context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) from the request ctx and returns without waiting. The request ctx is cancelled once the HTTP handler returns, so the derived context is cancelled with it. The 10s timeout therefore only matters if the request is still alive. The legacy call usually sees a cancelled context and fails, or never runs. The legacy store silently stops receiving writes in mode 3, and the failure is only recorded as a metric. I did not check how the legacy store handles a cancelled context. Also, Update passes the original objInfo to Legacy.Update, whereas the old code passed an updateWrapper carrying the object already written to Storage. So the legacy store recomputes the update against its own copy and can diverge from Storage.
